title: Public mint lures
takeaway: The public mint happens only on the official site, at the announced price and time. Nothing early, cheaper or "pay to verify" is real.

cards.title: A spot before everyone else?
cards.body: The public mint opens soon. Then a DM arrives. It knows the date and the price, it sounds friendly, and it offers you a guaranteed egg before everyone else for a small payment first.

seg.label: Friendly greeting
seg.why: Friendly words are not the problem.

seg: You have a guaranteed public mint spot.

seg.label: Pay first request
seg.why: No real mint asks you to send ETH to someone first.

seg.label: Unofficial mint site
seg.why: Not announced by the official accounts.

cards.title: How the public mint works
cards.body: On Nov 30 at 16:00 UTC the public mint opens for 2 hours. It is first come, first served, at 0.029 ETH an egg. There is no auction and no bidding, and eggs that do not sell are burned. It happens only on the official site.
points: Mint links come only from the official accounts.

cards.title: Pay to verify is always a lure
cards.body: No real mint, spot or prize makes you send ETH, a fee or a deposit to anyone first. The only cost is the mint price and the normal network fee, shown in your own wallet, on the official site. A DM saying you have a spot is not a spot.
points: Links in replies are not official.

cards.title: Dragon Guard has nothing to claim
cards.body: Scammers borrow any trusted name, even this course. Dragon Guard has no badge to claim, no NFT, no wallet step. A Guardian NFT or Dragon Guard reward link is a lure. pdtools will never ask for your wallet, your seed phrase or a signature.
points: No pdtools page asks for your wallet.

questions.stem: The public mint price is 0.029 ETH an egg. A site offers early eggs for 0.015 ETH. What is it?
options: A scam, there is no early or cheaper mint
A presale the team forgot to post
A real discount for loyal Keepers
Fine if it shows the dragon art
questions.why: The official post set one price, 0.029 ETH, on the official site at 16:00 UTC on Nov 30. Anything early or cheaper is a lure.

questions.stem: Tap every red flag, then Done.

seg.label: Greeting
seg.why: A greeting is not the problem.

seg.label: Unasked support message
seg.why: Real support never DMs you first.

seg.label: Send gas first
seg.why: A mint never needs you to send ETH to someone first.

seg.label: Stranger's address
seg.why: Sending to this address only pays the scammer.

questions.why: Support never DMs first, and no mint needs you to send ETH to an address. Check the official site from your bookmark.

questions.stem: A DM says you won a guaranteed public mint spot and must claim within 10 minutes. What do you do?
options: Ignore it and check the official site yourself
Claim fast, mint spots do need claiming
Reply to ask if it is real
Share the link in chat to check first
questions.why: The public mint is first come, first served on the official site. There are no spots to claim by DM.

questions.stem: A mint page asks you to send 0.01 ETH to verify your wallet before you can mint. What is this?
options: A scam, real claims never need payment first
A normal network fee for the claim
A safety step the team added
Fine if the page has a lock icon
questions.why: Sending ETH to verify is always a scam. The real mint only shows the price and the normal network fee in your own wallet.

questions.stem: Someone shares a link to claim a free Dragon Guard Guardian NFT. What do you do?
options: Ignore it, Dragon Guard has nothing to claim
Claim it, you earned it by finishing lessons
Connect only your mint wallet to claim
Ask the sender to share the contract
questions.why: Dragon Guard has no badge to claim, no NFT, no wallet step. Any Guardian NFT link is a lure.

questions.stem: Tap every red flag, then Done.

seg.label: Thank you message
seg.why: Thanks alone is not the problem.

seg.label: Unannounced mint site
seg.why: Not announced in advance on official channels.

questions.why: The rushed deadline and a mint site never announced in advance are the signs. Check on a second official channel.

questions.stem: You want to be ready for the public mint. Where will the real mint page come from?
options: The official Pocket Dragons accounts, announced in advance
The first reply under the mint post
A DM from an admin who wants to help
A search ad for a Pocket Dragons mint
questions.why: Trust only links from the official Pocket Dragons accounts, checked on two channels and announced in advance.

questions.stem: A reply under the official mint post offers a faster mint link. What do you do?
options: Ignore it, replies are not official channels
Use it if it has many likes
Use it if the name looks official
Try it with a small amount
questions.why: Anyone can reply under a post and copy a name. Replies are where fake links hide.

questions.why: The domain was never announced, and the page asks you to pay to verify. Close it and check the official accounts.

questions.stem: A stranger's mint site opens a wallet request that says Permit and names a spender. What do you do?
options: Reject it and close the site
Sign it, mints need permits
Sign it, signatures cost no gas
Sign it, then revoke later
questions.why: A Permit signature can let the spender take your tokens without gas. Minting never needs one from a stranger's site.
